problem:
A particle $P$ is moving in the $x$-$y$ plane. Its position vector relative to a fixed origin $O$ is given by

$$
r=⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle at time $t=\frac{\pi }{2}.$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Velocity for Plane Motion Using Differentiation

feedback.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+3),\,\sqrt{t}⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed $|v|$ of the particle at time $t=1.$ Do not round the answer.

The speed at time $t=1$ is
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity vector $v.$ Differentiating the position vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+3)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t+3},\,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=1,$ we substitute in the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =⟨\frac{1}{1+3},\,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1}}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{4},\,\frac{1}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the speed at $t=1$ we calculate the magnitude of $v(1),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|v(1)| & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{4})}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{16}+\frac{1}{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{5}{16}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
